notes: Pinned official guidance for the professional harness audit. Entries were recorded offline on 2026-09-20 from published vendor documentation, so each 'proposition' is the auditor's restatement of documented behaviour rather than a verbatim quotation, and 'content_hash' stays empty until a reviewed refresh fetches the page and fills it in. 'min_cli_version'/'max_cli_version' record the CLI generation an entry was reviewed against; widen a range only in a reviewed refresh, never at audit time. The audit performs no live request: refreshing this file is a tracked data change.

sources.title: Claude Code - Manage Claude's memory
sources.proposition: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md memory at separate user, project and local scopes, recursing up from the working directory and supporting imports of other files, so the same rule can reach a session from more than one scope.

sources.title: Claude Code settings
sources.proposition: Claude Code settings resolve from enterprise, command-line, local project, shared project and user settings files in a documented precedence order, so a lower-precedence setting can be present on disk yet shadowed and ineffective.

sources.title: Claude Code identity and access management
sources.proposition: Tool permissions are granted through allow, ask and deny rules in the settings files, and managed policy settings override user and project permission rules.

sources.title: Claude Code agent skills
sources.proposition: Skills are discovered from personal, project and plugin skill directories, and only a skill's name and description are loaded up front; the body is read when the skill is invoked, so an installed skill is not the same as loaded context.

sources.title: Claude Code hooks reference
sources.proposition: Hooks are registered in the settings files against named lifecycle events with matchers, and they run shell commands with the invoking user's permissions, so a hook whose event or matcher never fires is registered but ineffective.

sources.title: Claude Code slash commands
sources.proposition: Custom slash commands are Markdown files under a personal commands directory or a project commands directory, and a project command shadows a personal command of the same name.

sources.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
sources.proposition: MCP servers are configured at local, project or user scope, a project-scoped server requires approval before it is used, and an unauthenticated or unreachable server exposes no tools to the session.

sources.title: Claude Code CLI reference
sources.proposition: Command-line flags select which setting sources, tools and permissions a run uses, so the invocation - not only the files on disk - determines what actually reaches a session.

sources.title: Codex CLI
sources.proposition: The Codex CLI runs locally and takes project guidance from AGENTS.md files together with the user's global instructions, so a project file and a global file can both reach the same run.

sources.title: Codex configuration reference
sources.proposition: Codex settings live in config.toml inside CODEX_HOME (~/.codex by default), and command-line overrides take precedence over the file, so a key written to a config file that the run does not use has no effect.

sources.title: Codex sandbox and approval settings
sources.proposition: Codex restricts file writes and network access through a sandbox mode combined with an approval policy, and both are configurable per run, so the effective permissions of a Codex session come from that pair rather than from a single setting.

sources.title: openai/codex repository
sources.proposition: The openai/codex repository is the official distribution of the Codex CLI and the authoritative record of released versions and the documentation bundled with each one, which is what a version-pinned audit check is compared against.
